children: GameStop Corp. (GME, Financials), the video game retailer striving to rebuild its company, just earned a way stronger vote of confidence from Ryan Cohen.
The company's chairman and CEO purchased 1 million shares in the open market for around $20.3 million. His purchases ranged from $20.02 to $20.47 for a weighted average price of $20.3759 a share.
Shares gained more than 3% in premarket trade on Friday. The size of the purchase is noteworthy. The timing makes it more intriguing.
Cohen now directly owns around 39.3 million shares, increasing his financial exposure to a corporation that still has to prove what comes next after its traditional retail strategy.
The purchase comes after a nearly $1 million open-market purchase earlier this week by a GameStop director. Insider buying doesn't fix the firm itself.
But it can make a difference when high-level executives are putting their own money in, especially at a firm where investors are still waiting for a clearer long-term plan.
GameStop recently recorded net sales of $790.2 million for the second quarter, with collectibles making up a bigger part of the business.

Cohen's purchase raises the stakes for investors. Next, we will see whether his increasing personal dedication is matched with operating progress strong enough to alter how the market prices GameStop.

title: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen Buys $20.3M in Stock
